name: Vichela
body:
The vichela are an advanced race that has recently joined the larger galactic society in their reality after years of adaptation and gene manipulation to make them more humanoid. With most of their focus given to changing themselves physically, the vichela put far less time into space travel, and thus have only now pushed beyond the boundaries of their homeworld. This is reflected largely in the simplistic stylings of their culture despite mastering the intricacies of traveling between planets.

Physical Description: The vichela were originally more akin to the bees commonly found on many core worlds. Generations of blending their genetics with that of smaller humanoids have given them what they feel is a more acceptable appearance. They can stand on two legs, and generally prefer to use only two of their arms except when necessary to emulate humans, elves, and similar species.

Society: The vichela have modeled their society off of their research into the history of other beings. They have queen, ladies, duchesses, and countesses who rule over smaller and smaller pieces of society and report back up the chain. All leadership is feminine in capacity as far as other cultures are concerned, but with their splicing and alteration abilities, the designation is more a formality than a literal requirement.

Relations: Originally, vichela were parasitic; growing on and within larger creatures that inhabit their world. After developing sapience, they were aghast to learn what their occupation did to their hosts, so they set out to correct it. Many ages later, the vichela now reproduce much as other humanoids; which also allows them to better relate to their new peers. As long as they can find at least some benefit to their people in an agreement, the vichela are willing to agree to most deals. This extends to individual vichela as well, whose allegiances have been known to shift when a better offer is made for their partnership. Personal attachment exists, but can be hard to maintain without great effort on the part of those involved.

Alignment and Religion: Vichela society is generally seen as lawful, although their laws can waver as leadership changes and more beneficial deals are made to improve their society. On the other hand, the chaotic nature of their willingness to change their own DNA and perception of the world around them could take a larger role in some than others. There is no direct religious belief practiced by vichela as a whole; but individuals will join a church or cult if doing so gives them some greater purpose or aids them with their needs.

Adventurers: Vichela adventurers are great as contracted guides, mercenaries, and rangers, and they’re not above assassination for the right price. Males are most often guards and leave their homes less often than females looking for recognition; but again, the fluidity of the vichela’s roles in their society can and often does break this.

Vichela Names: Vichela take their names very seriously, trying to avoid pun-focused titles. They prefer to acquire archaic and outdated names from the other societies with whom they interact, and may take on different monickers between groups who know them. This can confuse anybody who travels with the vichela between locations, but the vichela themselves are widely known for their ability to remember and keep straight who they are in the eyes of different people.

Vichela Ancestry Traits (11 RP)
Ability Score Modifiers (0 RP): Vichela are very intelligent and agile, but years of modifications to their physical being has left them a little unstable. They gain +2 Dexterity and +2 Intelligence but suffer –2 Constitution.
Size Small (0 RP): Vichela are Small creatures and gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty on combat maneuver checks and to their Combat Maneuver Defense, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.
Speed (–1 RP): Slow. Vichela have a base speed of 20 feet.
Insectile Humanoid (0 RP): Vichela are humanoids with the insectile subtype.
Darkvision (2 RP): Vichela have Darkvision out to 60 feet.
Gliding Wings (3 RP): Vichela take no damage from falling (as if subject to a constant non-magical feather fall spell). While in midair, a vichela can move up to 5 feet in any horizontal direction for every 1 foot they fall, at a speed of 60 feet per round. A vichela with gliding wings cannot gain height with these wings alone; it merely coasts in other directions as it falls. If subjected to a strong wind or any other effect that causes a creature with gliding wings to rise, it can take advantage of the updraft to increase the distance it can glide.
Hybrid Stinger (4 RP): Vichela science has moved their stingers to their wrists, granting the vichela a sting natural attack. This is a primary attack in the light blade weapon group that deals 1d2 piercing damage on a hit. On a critical hit, the vichela can break off its stinger in its opponent, dealing 2d6 Constitution damage to itself and the target (no save). At 5th, 11th, and 17th level, this damage increases by 1d6, to a maximum of 5d6 Constitution damage at 17th level. After breaking off its stinger, the vichela loses its stinger attack for one week, or until it can be regenerated.
Quick Draw (2 RP): A vichela’s additional arms can be used to quickly retrieve their equipment, but aren’t much use in direct combat. They gain Quick Draw as a bonus feat.
Languages (1 RP): Vichela begin play speaking Common and Auran. Vichela with high Intelligence scores can choose any languages they want (except secret languages, such as Druidic).
Aging Effects
Adult	Middle Age	Old	Venerable	Maximum Age
20	50	80	130	+6d20 years
Physical Appearance
Base Height	Base Weight	Modifier	Weight Modifier
Male	2 ft. 6 in.	25 lbs.	2d6 x1
Female	2 ft. 8 in.	30 lbs.	2d6 x1
Vichela Queen Traits

Queens are vichela who have been born or altered to be larger and tougher than others of their species. They have all the same traits as other vichela, except as noted here.

Ability Score Modifiers +2 Strength, +2 Intelligence: Queens are stronger than most vichela, and equally as smart.
Size: Medium: As medium creatures, vichela queens have no benefits or penalty due to their size.
Speed: A vichela queen’s speed is 30 feet.
Gliding Wings: A vichela queen has no wings.
Hybrid Stinger: This functions as the vichela, but deals 1d3 base piercing damage instead because of the queen’s size.
Alternate Ancestry Traits
Bio-Manipulation (2 RP): A vichela can make its secondary pair of arms useless in order to improve its physical toughness. These vichela do not take a penalty to their Constitution score. This alters the vichela’s ability scores and replaces Quick Draw.
Wasp Stinger (3 RP): A vichela can develop the use of its wrist stinger at the cost of its wings. The stinger on these vichela deals 1d4 piercing damage with a critical threat range of 19-20 x2. They can continue to use their stinger after breaking off the end, but still cannot break it off again until it grows back naturally or through regeneration. This replaces gliding wings.
Toxicity (2 RP): Vichela that live in the open and away from their hive-like cities have adapted their senses and stingers for greater survival. These vichela have low-light vision, and gain the following extraordinary ability: A number of times per day equal to its Constitution modifier (minimum 1/day), the vichela can envenom a weapon that it wields in the hand with its wrist stinger (using venom from the stinger). Applying venom in this way is a swift action. This replaces Darkvision.
Life-Stealing Venom—Injury; save Fort DC 10 + 1/2 the vichela’s level + its Constitution modifier; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1 Con; cure 1 save.
Vichela Weapon Familiarity (2 RP): Vichela society enjoys old-fashioned weaponry more than modern firearms and blasters. A vichela with this ancestry trait is proficient in two piercing weapons of its choice. This replaces Quick Draw.
Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist: Add +1 on Craft (alchemy) checks to craft poison and +1/3 on the DCs of poisons the alchemist creates.
Gladiator, Theian: Add +2 on rolls to stabilize when dying.
Key Guardian: Add +1/3 on critical hit confirmation rolls with a keyblade of the key guardian’s choice (maximum bonus +5). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Makari: Add +1/3 on critical hit confirmation rolls made using weapons with which the makari can apply Weapon Finesse (maximum bonus of +5). This does not stack with Critical Focus.
Marshal: Add the marshal’s Charisma bonus (if any) against 1/5 additional attacks each round after issuing a defense command with precise orders.
Mercenary: Add +1/4 to the DC of moral ambiguity. At +1, you gain that class feature.
Noble, Theian: Gain 1/6 of a new paragon noble talent.
Ranger: If the ranger has gliding wings, add a +1 racial bonus on Fly skill checks. When this bonus reaches +8, the ranger gains a fly speed of 15 feet with poor maneuverability (this does not grant the ranger another +8 racial bonus on Fly checks).
Rogue: Add +1/3 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using sneak attack (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
